title: Geography Lec 2
summary: India is divided into six physiographic divisions; the largest is the Peninsular Plateau.
Himalaya: Trans Himalaya (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar), Greater Himalaya (average 6000 m), Lesser (Middle) Himalaya and Shiwaliks (Outer); Duns lie between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks.
In the Northeast the Shiwaliks are replaced by the Duars, famous for tea gardens.
Alignment of the Himalaya: NW to SE in Kashmir, east-west in Sikkim-Darjeeling, and NE to SW in the Purvanchal region.
Major peaks: Everest 8848 m, K2 8611 m (Karakoram, PoK), Kanchenjunga 8598 m (highest in India), Lhotse 8516 m, Nanda Devi 7816 m (Uttarakhand).
Siachen is the longest glacier of the Karakoram; Operation Meghdoot was carried out in Siachen.
Purvanchal (Himalayan): Dafla, Miri, Abor, Mishmi, Patkai, Barail, Naga, Manipur, Mizo hills; Garo-Khasi-Jaintia, Mikir and Rengma hills are part of the Peninsular Plateau.
The Himalaya is about 50 million years old (young fold mountains); the Aravalli is about 500 million years old.
Passes: Shipki La (Sutlej), Rohtang, Bara-lacha La (Himachal); Banihal (J&K), Burzil (to Gilgit), Zoji La (to Leh); Mig La is the highest motorable pass.
Western Ghats: higher (about 1200 m), continuous, highest peak Anamudi 2695 m; Eastern Ghats: about 600 m, discontinuous; the two meet at the Nilgiris.
Peninsular Plateau: Central Highlands north of the Narmada, Deccan Plateau to the south; the Rajmahal Hills form the eastern edge, followed by the Malda Gap and the Meghalaya Plateau.
Major peaks: Guru Shikhar (Aravalli, 1722 m), Dhupgarh (Satpura), Amarkantak (Maikal), Parasnath (Chota Nagpur, 1365 m), Kalsubai (Maharashtra).
Coastal plains: western is narrow, submerged and indented; eastern is broad, emergent, with deltas and lagoons.
Northern Plains: Bhabar (8-16 km), Terai (15-30 km), Bhangar (old alluvium), Khadar (new alluvium); length within India about 2400 km.

Islands: 9° Channel (Lakshadweep-Minicoy), 8° Channel (Minicoy-Maldives), 10° Channel (Andaman-Nicobar); Barren is an active volcano, Narcondam dormant; Andrott is the largest and Bitra the smallest island of Lakshadweep.

mcqs.q: India is divided into how many physiographic divisions?
mcqs.e: Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Thar Desert, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains and Islands.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest physiographic division of India?
mcqs.e: The Peninsular Plateau is the largest physiographic division.

mcqs.q: How many lines of latitude are there in total on the Earth?
mcqs.e: 90 in each hemisphere plus the Equator make 181 (the poles count as points).

mcqs.q: How many latitudinal circles are there?
mcqs.e: The poles are points, not circles, so 181 - 2 = 179.

mcqs.q: Which is the most densely populated desert in the world?
mcqs.e: The Thar lies to the northwest of the Aravalli.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Himalaya is correct?
o: It is not one range but a series of several parallel ranges
It is just a single peak
mcqs.e: Trans Himalaya, Greater, Lesser and Shiwalik: several parallel ranges.

mcqs.q: Which ranges form the Trans Himalaya (from north to south)?
mcqs.e: Towards Tibet this chain is known as the Kailash Range.

mcqs.q: Which two landmasses were formed by the break-up of Pangaea?
mcqs.e: India was part of Gondwanaland; the surrounding ocean was Panthalassa.

mcqs.q: Which sea existed earlier in place of the Himalaya?
mcqs.e: The Tethys was a geosyncline where sediments were deposited.

mcqs.q: The Himalaya was formed by the collision of which plates?
mcqs.e: The Indian Plate drifted north from the Southern Hemisphere and collided with Eurasia.

mcqs.q: Why does the Himalaya have several parallel ranges?
o: Due to repeated phases of collision and uplift
mcqs.e: Successive phases of compression produced several parallel ranges.

mcqs.q: What is the Pamir Knot called?
mcqs.e: The Tibetan Plateau is also called the Roof of the World.

mcqs.q: Which mountain ranges converge at the Pamir Knot?
mcqs.e: The Hindu Kush lies in Afghanistan-Pakistan, not in India.

mcqs.q: Which is the innermost range of the Himalaya?
mcqs.e: The Greater Himalaya is also called the Inner Himalaya.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Lesser Himalaya known?
mcqs.e: It is also called the Himachal.

mcqs.q: By what other name are the Shiwaliks known?
mcqs.e: The Shiwaliks are the outermost and lowest range.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate average height of the Greater Himalaya?
mcqs.e: Greater Himalaya is the highest; Lesser about 4000 m and Shiwalik about 1000 m.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate average height of the Shiwaliks?
mcqs.e: The Shiwalik is the lowest Himalayan range.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate average width of the Greater Himalaya?
mcqs.e: The Greater Himalaya is very high but only about 25 km wide on average.

mcqs.q: Which range of the Himalaya is largely absent in the Northeast (towards Arunachal)?
mcqs.e: The Duars occupy the place of the Shiwaliks here.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'Duar' mean?
mcqs.e: The Duars are famous for tea gardens and replace the Shiwaliks.

mcqs.q: The longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks are called:
mcqs.e: Examples: Dehradun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest Dun valley?
mcqs.e: Dehradun lies between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks.

mcqs.q: What does 'Doab' mean?
mcqs.e: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.

mcqs.q: The Raichur Doab lies between which two rivers?
mcqs.e: It was a disputed region between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms.

mcqs.q: The Atal Tunnel is built in which Himalayan range?
mcqs.e: It is 9.02 km long and lies in Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The Atal Tunnel connects:
mcqs.e: It is an alternative to the Rohtang Pass, which also links Manali and Lahaul.

mcqs.q: In which part of the Himalaya is the variation in altitude the greatest?
mcqs.e: E.g. in Sikkim, Kanchenjunga rises close to very low hills.

mcqs.q: In which direction does the Himalaya extend in Jammu and Kashmir?
mcqs.e: In Sikkim-Darjeeling the alignment is roughly east-west.

mcqs.q: In which direction does the Himalaya trend in Arunachal (Eastern Himalaya)?
mcqs.e: Here the ranges take a sharp bend towards the Purvanchal hills.

mcqs.q: Which glacier in the Karakoram is the world's second longest outside the polar regions?
mcqs.e: The longest non-polar glacier is the Fedchenko in Tajikistan.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest glacier in the world?
mcqs.e: It lies in the polar region; the Fedchenko is the longest non-polar glacier.

mcqs.q: In which country is the Fedchenko Glacier located?
mcqs.e: It is the longest non-polar glacier.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Karakoram glacier?
mcqs.e: Gangotri is in the Greater Himalaya in Uttarakhand; Siachen is also in the Karakoram.

mcqs.q: Where was Operation Meghdoot carried out?
mcqs.e: Launched by the Indian Army in 1984; Siachen is the world's highest battlefield.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak in the world?
mcqs.e: About 8848 m, on the Nepal-Tibet (China) border.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate height of Mount Everest?
mcqs.e: It lies on the Nepal-Tibet (China) border.

mcqs.q: What is the other name of K2?
mcqs.e: 8611 m high, in the Karakoram in PoK (Gilgit-Baltistan).

mcqs.q: What is the height of K2?
mcqs.e: It is the second highest peak in the world.

mcqs.q: In which mountain range is K2 located?
mcqs.e: Everest and Kanchenjunga are in the Greater Himalaya, but K2 is in the Karakoram.

mcqs.q: Excluding PoK, which is the highest peak in India?
mcqs.e: Located in Sikkim, height 8598 m.

mcqs.q: In which state is Kanchenjunga located?
mcqs.e: It is the third highest peak in the world.

mcqs.q: Which is the third highest peak in the world?
mcqs.e: The fourth is Lhotse (about 8516 m).

mcqs.q: What is the approximate height of Lhotse?
mcqs.e: Fourth highest peak in the world, on the Nepal-Tibet border.

mcqs.q: In which country are the Makalu, Dhaulagiri and Annapurna peaks?
mcqs.e: They lie in the Greater Himalaya in Nepal.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Uttarakhand?
mcqs.e: 7816 m; the highest peak lying entirely within India.

mcqs.q: What is the height of Nanda Devi?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Greater Himalaya in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: In which state is Mount Kamet?
mcqs.e: About 7756 m; second highest peak of Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: What does 'Dhaulagiri' mean?
mcqs.e: Dhaulagiri is a peak in Nepal, while Dhauladhar is a range in Himachal.

mcqs.q: What is the Dhauladhar?
o: The local name of the Lesser Himalaya in Himachal Pradesh
mcqs.e: Pir Panjal in Kashmir, Nag Tibba in Uttarakhand, Mahabharat Range in Nepal.

mcqs.q: By what name is the Lesser Himalaya known in Uttarakhand?
mcqs.e: In Nepal it is called the Mahabharat Range.

mcqs.q: By what name is the Lesser Himalaya known in Nepal?
mcqs.e: Pir Panjal in Kashmir and Dhauladhar in Himachal.

mcqs.q: From west to east, the Himalaya extends between which rivers?
mcqs.e: The Indus in the west and the Brahmaputra (Dihang) in the east.

mcqs.q: What are the summer grasslands of Uttarakhand called?
mcqs.e: The Bhotiya tribe lives in this region.

mcqs.q: Which tribe is found in the Bugyal region of Uttarakhand?
mcqs.e: Bugyals are summer grasslands.

mcqs.q: What are 'Karewas' in the Kashmir Himalaya?
mcqs.e: They are considered good for saffron cultivation.

mcqs.q: Karewas are suitable for which crop?
mcqs.e: A special landform of the Kashmir Himalaya.

mcqs.q: In the river-based division of the Himalaya, the part between the Indus and the Sutlej is called:
mcqs.e: Kumaon: Sutlej-Kali; Nepal: Kali-Teesta; Assam: Teesta-Dihang.

mcqs.q: Which Himalayan section lies between the Sutlej and the Kali rivers?
mcqs.e: It covers the Kumaon-Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: Which Himalayan section lies between the Kali and the Teesta rivers?
mcqs.e: The Assam Himalaya lies between the Teesta and the Dihang.

mcqs.q: Which Himalayan section lies between the Teesta and the Dihang (Brahmaputra)?
mcqs.e: Beyond this begin the Purvanchal hills.

mcqs.q: In which range is the Fotu La pass located?
mcqs.e: It is in Ladakh, on the Srinagar-Leh highway.

mcqs.q: Which is the world's highest motorable pass (as taught in the lecture)?
mcqs.e: In eastern Ladakh, about 5913 m high.

mcqs.q: Where is the Mig La pass located?
mcqs.e: Earlier Umling La was considered the highest.

mcqs.q: Which of the following are passes of Uttarakhand?
mcqs.e: Uttarakhand's passes lie on the border with Tibet (China).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a pass of Arunachal Pradesh?
mcqs.e: Nathu La and Jelep La are in Sikkim.

mcqs.q: Which of the following are passes of Sikkim?
mcqs.e: Nathu La is an India-China trade route.

mcqs.q: Where is the Diphu Pass located?
mcqs.e: Other Arunachal passes: Bum La, Bomdi La, Yonggyap, Dihang.

mcqs.q: Through which pass does the Sutlej enter India?
mcqs.e: Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The Rohtang Pass connects:
mcqs.e: The Atal Tunnel is its tunnel alternative.

mcqs.q: The Bara-lacha La connects:
mcqs.e: Three key passes of Himachal: Shipki La, Rohtang, Bara-lacha La.

mcqs.q: The Banihal Pass connects:
mcqs.e: It lies in the Pir Panjal Range.

mcqs.q: The Burzil Pass connects:
mcqs.e: It lies on the Srinagar-Gilgit route.

mcqs.q: The Zoji La connects:
mcqs.e: It lies on the Srinagar-Kargil-Leh route.

mcqs.q: In which range/region are the Mintaka and Aghil passes?
mcqs.e: They are passes on the northern frontier.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the Purvanchal hills?
mcqs.e: Garo-Khasi-Jaintia hills are part of the Peninsular Plateau.

mcqs.q: What is the other name of the Mizo Hills?
mcqs.e: They are part of the Purvanchal (Himalayan) system.

mcqs.q: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills are part of:
mcqs.e: The Meghalaya Plateau is also called the Shillong Plateau.

mcqs.q: The Mikir and Rengma hills are part of:
mcqs.e: They are located in Assam.

mcqs.q: What type of mountains is the Himalaya?
mcqs.e: About 40-50 million years old.

mcqs.q: Approximately how old is the Aravalli range considered to be?
mcqs.e: One of the oldest fold mountains in the world, about ten times older than the Himalaya.

mcqs.q: Which Indian mountain range is among the oldest fold mountains in the world?
mcqs.e: The Aravalli forms the northwestern edge of the Peninsular Plateau.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
mcqs.e: 2695 m; also the highest peak of South India.

mcqs.q: In which state and range is Anamudi located?
mcqs.e: The Western Ghats are highest in the Kerala region.

mcqs.q: What is the height of Anamudi?
mcqs.e: Highest peak of South India.

mcqs.q: Doddabetta, a major peak of the Western Ghats, lies in which range?
mcqs.e: It is the highest peak of the Nilgiris, near Ooty in Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: In which state is Doddabetta located?
mcqs.e: It is the highest peak of the Nilgiris.

mcqs.q: Which are the major hill ranges of the southern Western Ghats?
mcqs.e: Anamudi is in the Anamalai and Doddabetta in the Nilgiri hills.

mcqs.q: Which peak lies in the northern part of the Eastern Ghats?
mcqs.e: Height about 1501 m.

mcqs.q: Which is considered the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats?
mcqs.e: Height about 1680-1690 m, in the Visakhapatnam hills.

mcqs.q: On which hills is the Tirupati Balaji temple located?
mcqs.e: Part of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a hill of the Eastern Ghats?
mcqs.e: Anamalai is in the Western Ghats.

mcqs.q: The average heights of the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats are respectively about:
mcqs.e: The Western Ghats are higher, and their height increases from north to south.

mcqs.q: In which direction does the height of the Western Ghats increase?
mcqs.e: The highest peaks are in the south (Kerala).

mcqs.q: Which Ghats are continuous?
mcqs.e: The Eastern Ghats are cut through by rivers at several places.

mcqs.q: Why are the Eastern Ghats discontinuous?
o: Erosion by rivers, as the plateau slopes eastwards
mcqs.e: The Peninsular Plateau tilts east, so most rivers flow east and cut through the Eastern Ghats.

mcqs.q: The Western Ghats extend across how many states?
mcqs.e: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: When were the Western Ghats declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
mcqs.e: Famous for their biodiversity.

mcqs.q: When is the International Day for Biological Diversity observed?
mcqs.e: 22 March is World Water Day, 22 April is Earth Day.

mcqs.q: When is World Water Day observed?
mcqs.e: Earth Day is observed on 22 April.

mcqs.q: When is World Earth Day observed?
mcqs.e: Biodiversity Day is 22 May.

mcqs.q: Which hill station is in the Nilgiri Hills?
mcqs.e: The Western and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiris.

mcqs.q: Where do the Western and Eastern Ghats meet?
mcqs.e: Doddabetta is located here.

mcqs.q: Which pass lies between the Nilgiri and the Anamalai hills?
mcqs.e: It links Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: Bhor Ghat connects which cities?
mcqs.e: Bhor Ghat links Mumbai with Pune; Thal Ghat links Mumbai with Nashik.

mcqs.q: Thal Ghat connects which cities?
mcqs.e: Bhor Ghat connects Mumbai and Pune.

mcqs.q: The Peninsular Plateau is mainly made up of which rocks?
o: Ancient crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks
mcqs.e: Black soil is found in the Deccan Trap (volcanic) region.

mcqs.q: The Narmada divides the Peninsular Plateau into which two parts?
mcqs.e: The Deccan Plateau is shaped like an inverted triangle.

mcqs.q: What is the shape of the Deccan Plateau?
mcqs.e: It lies to the south of the Narmada.

mcqs.q: Which plateau lies to the north of the Narmada?
mcqs.e: Central Highlands include Mewar/Marwar, Malwa, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chota Nagpur.

mcqs.q: What is the typical average height of a plateau and its main feature?
mcqs.e: Unlike mountains, a plateau has no pointed summit.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Central Highlands?
mcqs.e: The Central Highlands lie north of the Narmada; the Maharashtra Plateau is part of the Deccan.

mcqs.q: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is known as:
o: The Ruhr of India (storehouse of minerals)
mcqs.e: It is a mineral-rich region.

mcqs.q: The Ranchi and Hazaribagh plateaus are part of:
mcqs.e: The Damodar flows through this plateau.

mcqs.q: The Damodar river flows through which plateau?
mcqs.e: It is a tributary of the Hooghly.

mcqs.q: Which hills form the eastern edge of the main Peninsular Plateau, before the Malda Gap?
mcqs.e: Beyond them lies the Malda Gap, then the Meghalaya Plateau.

mcqs.q: The gap between the Rajmahal Hills and the Meghalaya Plateau is called:
mcqs.e: Here the plateau dips under the alluvium towards Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Meghalaya Plateau known?
mcqs.e: It includes the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills.

mcqs.q: In which state is the Karbi Anglong Plateau?
mcqs.e: The Mikir and Rengma hills are part of it.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the Shillong Plateau?
mcqs.e: The Maikal range is in central India where the Vindhya and Satpura meet.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Maikal Range?
mcqs.e: The Maikal is the junction of the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Satpura Range?
mcqs.e: In the Mahadeo Hills, about 1350 m high.

mcqs.q: What is the west-to-east order of the Satpura ranges?
mcqs.e: Asirgarh Fort is in Burhanpur (Madhya Pradesh).

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Vindhya Range?
mcqs.e: Also called Kalumar Peak, about 752 m high.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Chota Nagpur Plateau?
mcqs.e: In Giridih district of Jharkhand, about 1365 m high.

mcqs.q: Parasnath Hill is associated with which Jain Tirthankara?
mcqs.e: It is a Jain pilgrimage site (Shikharji).

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Aravalli?
mcqs.e: At Mount Abu, 1722 m high.

mcqs.q: In which mountain area is Guru Shikhar located?
mcqs.e: Highest peak of the Aravalli.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Maharashtra?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Sahyadri (Western Ghats).

mcqs.q: Anamudi lies at the junction of which three hill ranges?
mcqs.e: It is part of the Anamalai Range.

mcqs.q: Why is the Peninsular Plateau considered geologically stable?
o: It is a young fold mountain system
It is an ancient shield with low seismic activity
mcqs.e: It lies away from plate boundaries, whereas the Himalaya lies on one and has frequent earthquakes.

mcqs.q: Which fault in the Peninsular Plateau is known for frequent seismic activity?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Maharashtra-Karnataka region.

mcqs.q: When did the devastating earthquake strike Bhuj in Gujarat?
mcqs.e: Though the peninsula is stable, the Kutch region is seismically active.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a major part of the Peninsular Plateau?
mcqs.e: The Purvanchal is part of the Himalayan system.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of the Western Coastal Plain?
mcqs.e: It has more natural harbours.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of the Eastern Coastal Plain?
o: Broad, emergent, with depositional features and deltas
mcqs.e: The western coast is narrow with natural harbours.

mcqs.q: An indented coastline with natural harbours is a feature of which coast?
mcqs.e: The east coast has more artificial harbours.

mcqs.q: What is the coast of Karnataka called?
mcqs.e: Konkan for Maharashtra-Goa; Malabar for Kerala.

mcqs.q: What is the coast of Maharashtra and Goa called?
mcqs.e: Konkani is spoken in Goa.

mcqs.q: By what name is the coast of Kerala known?
mcqs.e: The Kathiawar coast lies in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: What is the coast of Tamil Nadu called?
mcqs.e: The Andhra coast is called the Northern Circars.

mcqs.q: What is the coastal plain of Andhra Pradesh called?
mcqs.e: Odisha has the Utkal plain.

mcqs.q: What is the coastal plain of Odisha called?
mcqs.e: The West Bengal coast is called the Bengal coast.

mcqs.q: What is the coast of Gujarat called?
mcqs.e: Beyond the Rann of Kutch lies Saurashtra/Kathiawar.

mcqs.q: What is the width of the Bhabar belt?
mcqs.e: A narrow belt where streams disappear underground.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of the Bhabar belt?
o: Pebble-studded zone where rivers go underground
mcqs.e: It lies at the foot of the Shiwaliks.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate width of the Terai belt?
mcqs.e: Here the streams re-emerge.

mcqs.q: Which best describes the Terai belt?
o: Marshy, densely forested zone where streams re-emerge
mcqs.e: The Terai lies south of the Bhabar.

mcqs.q: What is Khadar?
mcqs.e: Renewed by floods every year, hence more fertile.

mcqs.q: What is Bhangar?
mcqs.e: It contains calcareous nodules (kankar).

mcqs.q: Which is more fertile, Khadar or Bhangar, and why?
o: Khadar, because it is renewed by floods every year
Bhangar, because it has more kankar
mcqs.e: Khadar receives fresh silt every year.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate west-to-east length of the Northern Plains within India?
mcqs.e: The total length including Pakistan and Bangladesh is about 3200 km.

mcqs.q: The Northern Plains are formed by which three river systems?
mcqs.e: In that order from west to east.

mcqs.q: Why is canal irrigation more suitable in the Northern Plains?
o: Rivers flow only in the monsoon
mcqs.e: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra are glacier-fed and perennial.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct feature of the Northern Plains?
o: Bhabar, Terai and alluvial plains occur in sequence below the Shiwaliks
mcqs.e: Sequence: Shiwalik, Bhabar, Terai, alluvial plains.

mcqs.q: Which state has the highest population density (Census 2011)?
mcqs.e: About 1106 persons per sq km; West Bengal is second.

mcqs.q: Which hills lie immediately to the west of the Malda Gap?
mcqs.e: The Malda Gap separates the Rajmahal Hills from the Meghalaya (Garo) hills.

mcqs.q: Which Indian island group is closest to the Malabar coast?
mcqs.e: Lakshadweep falls under the Kerala High Court.

mcqs.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over Lakshadweep?

mcqs.q: The Palk Strait separates:
mcqs.e: The Gulf of Mannar lies to its south.

mcqs.q: The Nine Degree Channel separates:
mcqs.e: Minicoy is also part of the UT of Lakshadweep.

mcqs.q: The Eight Degree Channel separates:
mcqs.e: It marks the southern limit of Lakshadweep.

mcqs.q: The Eleven Degree Channel divides Lakshadweep into which two groups?

mcqs.q: The Ten Degree Channel separates:
mcqs.e: It lies between Little Andaman and Car Nicobar.

mcqs.q: Which waterway lies between Little Andaman and South Andaman?

mcqs.q: What is the status of the volcano on Narcondam Island?

mcqs.e: Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar are archipelagos.

mcqs.q: Which state has the longest coastline?
mcqs.e: Among states, Gujarat leads, followed by Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which Union Territory has the longest coastline?
mcqs.e: Nine states of India have a coastline.

mcqs.q: Which option is correct about the number of inhabited islands in Andaman and Nicobar?
mcqs.e: About 37-38 of the islands are inhabited.

mcqs.q: What is the main reason for the formation of lagoons on the east coast?
o: Deposition along the coast by rivers and wave action
mcqs.e: Chilika and Pulicat are examples.

mcqs.q: Under what conditions do coral reefs flourish?
o: In clear, saline, sunlit warm water
mcqs.e: Algae (zooxanthellae) inside the polyps carry out photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: Why do coral reefs not develop at river mouths?
o: Fresh, muddy water is unsuitable for them
mcqs.e: Corals need saline, clear water.

mcqs.q: In which coastal state are the plateau, plains and coastal plain all found?
mcqs.e: Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh are landlocked.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Mizoram?
mcqs.e: It is also called the Blue Mountain.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Tripura?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Jampui hills.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Arunachal Pradesh?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Eastern Himalaya.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of Meghalaya?
mcqs.e: It lies on the Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau.

mcqs.q: The Barail Range is part of:
mcqs.e: Dafla, Miri, Abor, Mishmi, Patkai Bum, Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills also belong to it.

mcqs.q: What topic was announced for the next day at the end of the lecture?
mcqs.e: Later topics: agriculture, soils, climate, and forests and grasslands.
